CausalChain: Hypoxia in the tumor microenvironment -> Enhanced exosome biogenesis and selective packaging of miR-155 -> Exosomal miR-155 transfer to neighboring cancer cells -> Downregulation of tumor-suppressive targets (such as TP53INP1 and GATA3) -> Induction and maintenance of EMT and cancer stem cell-like features -> Increased chemoresistance
Hypothesis: In hypoxic tumor environments, the selective exosomal packaging and intercellular transfer of miR-155 creates a self-reinforcing loop that promotes EMT and cancer stemness, leading to multidrug resistance; therefore, strategies aimed at inhibiting miR-155 exosomal sorting or release may reverse chemoresistance in cancer.
Abstract: Emerging evidence has highlighted that the interplay between exosome‐mediated microRNA (miRNA) transfer and the epithelial–mesenchymal transition (EMT) plays a critical role in drug resistance across various cancers. Recent studies indicate that hypoxic conditions within tumors can alter the miRNA composition of exosomes, potentially reinforcing EMT and cancer stem cell properties in adjacent cells. Here we propose a novel hypothesis that hypoxia‐induced exosomal delivery of miR‐155 establishes an intercellular feedback loop that both promotes EMT and fosters cancer stemness, thereby exacerbating chemoresistance. Targeting the process of miR‐155 sorting into exosomes or blocking its exosomal release may offer new therapeutic avenues to reverse drug resistance in malignancies.
